summary: This is one change you can attribute, inside the kernel being measured. The PTX m16n8k32 e4m3 fragment mapping in the spec is correct, and the numerics are within the rules. Two things are uncertain. ptxas may lower FP8 mma.sync on sm_90a to F2FP+HMMA instead of a native FP8 MMA. And the decode_32 'issue-bound' argument does not hold up. A flat result is still informative, so proceed as a medium-risk scored submit, but build in a fallback to the f16 v1 kernel.
justification: Mechanism. Kernel A at decode_16 is 111.4 us for ~329 MB (2.95 TB/s), against a 63.2 us floor. Per lane per 64-token tile it issues 16 cvt for K (8 calls of e4m3x4_to_f16x2x2), 16 cvt plus 8 prmt for V, and 8+8 mma.sync. It also does the softmax ex2/shfl work. The spec writes '8+16 mma'; the P@V count is actually 8 (2 hw x 4 j). The stage-1 review estimated ~40 us of cvt ALU that has to hide under the gather. Removing the K widening halves the cvt count, halves the QK mma count and frees 4 Q registers. If A is partly issue-bound, 5-10% on A is a fair upper bound. I checked the layout against the PTX m16n8k32 .e4m3 figures. A: a0 = row groupID, k 4*qi..+3; a1 = row +8; a2 = row groupID, k 16+4*qi..+3; a3 = row +8. B: b0 = k 4*qi..+3, b1 = k 16+4*qi..+3, col = groupID. C has the same f32 layout as m16n8k16. The proposed operands (a1 = a3 = 0, chunk index g*4 + ks*2 + {0,1} XOR (tt&7), byte offset 4*qi) match this. The K reads stay conflict-free: 8 tokens with distinct tt&7 x 4 qi words give 32 distinct banks. The once-per-item Q load is now a 4-way bank conflict, which costs almost nothing. Weakest link 1: native support on sm_90. FP8 mma.sync m16n8k32 is specified for sm_89+, but Hopper's documented FP8 tensor-core path is wgmma. ptxas may lower mma.sync e4m3 on sm_90a to F2FP conversions plus HMMA.16816. In that case the K cvt does not go away, and the Q operand could be re-converted every tile instead of once per item, which is flat or slower. I could not verify this here: there is no CUDA toolkit or GPU on this node. A flat A time therefore has two explanations: 'A is DRAM/TLB-bound', or 'the FP8 MMA was emulated'. Weakest link 2: decode_32. It runs at a lower bandwidth per byte (2.67 vs 2.95 TB/s), but its ALU work per byte is identical to decode_16. An issue-bound kernel would run at the same TB/s at both shapes. The drop as the footprint doubles (~350 -> ~700 MB of randomly permuted rows) points to TLB reach or DRAM row locality, not ALU. Expect decode_32 to gain no more than decode_16 in relative terms, likely less. The 225-235 us target is optimistic. Headline arithmetic: about 123 -> 116 us at decode_16 (load 2925 -> ~2813, 1.039x) and about 257.7 -> 240 us at decode_32 (load 5282 -> ~5000, 1.056x). That works out to only ~+1.6% on the 6-load geomean (1.347 -> ~1.37x), inside the +-1.5% CI and ~2% drift. Judge the run on kernel A's own top_kernels time against 111.4/245.5 us, not on the headline. Directions in `expected` are consistent with TASK.md: sliding, full decode_1 and every verify shape stay outside the gate and are byte-identical.
confounders: full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv (direct parent, same kernel): no confound. Only the QK operand path inside kernel A changes, and A's own time is read directly. Its pipeline depth (4 stages, 2 CTAs/SM, 128 KB in flight per SM) does decide whether A is issue-bound at all, so a flat result settles the question only for this pipeline configuration.

fused-preattention-triton: it produces the FP8 q bytes that now feed the MMA directly instead of being widened. It is the same numeric input as today, since widening e4m3 to f16 is exact, so there is no confound beyond tensor-core accumulation order.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing / paired-heads-launch-cleanup / -ab-tune-batch-gate / sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate: the gated path runs with PAIRED=False and never touches FA3 or the sliding kernel. They cannot interact.
interference: No companion is warranted. The result can be read directly from kernel A's profile row at decode_16/32 against the parent's 111.4/245.5 us; the shapes outside the gate are byte-identical. An ab-revert of the parent is impossible (the kernel is the parent). A control that splits 'drop Q cvt' from 'drop K cvt' does not make sense, because both come from one MMA instruction change. The one ambiguity a companion cannot fix is native vs emulated FP8 mma.sync on sm_90a. That needs a SASS check: before claiming, compile the CUDA string offline with nvcc -cubin -arch=sm_90a on any machine with CUDA 12.4+ (no GPU needed) and grep cuobjdump -sass for QMMA/HMMA and F2FP counts. Do not spawn a process from submission.py: that is a rules violation. If you cannot do the SASS check, record a flat A time as 'emulated-or-memory-bound' (undetermined), not as proof that A is DRAM-bound. Do not stop the ALU line of work on that basis alone.
rules_flags: None blocking. Q stays FP8 E4M3 (the allowed rounding, as FA3 does). K/V remain FP8 cache bytes used as-is. FP8 x FP8 products are exact, and accumulation is the tensor core's fp32 (Hopper FP8 accumulation keeps reduced internal precision, ~1e-4 relative on 64-term dots, far inside the 3% bound). No new host sync, allocation or caching of data-derived values. The build and self-check still run at import on synthetic data only.

Correctness hardening for a scored submit: keep the import-time self-check (3 configs, kv_scale 1 and 0.25, device grid and 3-CTA grid, rel L2 < 2e-2, finite). Change the fallback so a failed _v1fp8qk build or self-check falls back to the existing f16 muse_full_decode_splitkv_v1 kernel, keeping both CUDA source variants, then re-runs the self-check on it. It should not fall back to master FA3. Otherwise a ptxas rejection of e4m3 mma on sm_90a would score as a ~-4% regression of the landed 1.347x, not as flat. The second compile costs ~41 s only on failure, well inside the 15-minute budget.
The log must say which kernel ran (print '[splitkv] fp8-qk path active' or the fallback reason). The harvest has to read the log tail, per the existing DECISIONS note for this kernel.
open_questions: Does ptxas for sm_90a emit native FP8 MMA for mma.sync.m16n8k32.e4m3, or F2FP+HMMA emulation? This decides how to read a flat result. Check the SASS offline before or alongside the run.

Why is decode_32 at 2.67 TB/s vs decode_16 at 2.95 TB/s when its ALU work per byte is the same? That points to TLB reach or DRAM locality over the ~700 MB random footprint. If confirmed, the next lever is bytes in flight or access order (stages, CTAs/SM, chunk ordering for locality), not ALU.

Register count after the change (qa[4][2] -> 4 regs). If it drops well below the 128-reg cap of __launch_bounds__(256,2), would 3 CTAs/SM become possible? That is a separate follow-up, not part of this run.

Overlap with full-verify-cuda-streamk-splitkv (same FP8 op, same CUDA string). Whichever lands second rebases. This run's SASS and timing evidence on FP8 mma.sync should feed into that hypothesis's design.
